prompt: Which layer of the IoT architecture directly converts physical environmental phenomena into electrical voltage signals?
options: Perception / Sensing Layer
Network Ingestion Layer
Cloud Analytics Layer
Application Presentation Layer
explanation: The perception layer houses physical sensors (e.g. thermistors, photodiodes) that convert physical properties into electrical signals.

prompt: Why is the function 'delay(5000)' generally avoided in production embedded microcontroller code?
options: Because delay() consumes 100 times more battery power than active calculation.
Because delay() blocks the single execution thread completely, preventing the chip from responding to urgent sensor interrupts or network packets.
Because delay() can only be called inside the setup() function in C++.
Because microcontrollers crash if delay exceeds 1000 milliseconds.
explanation: Blocking delay pauses the CPU clock ticks. Using millis() time deltas allows the processor to remain responsive to asynchronous tasks.

prompt: According to the 'Iron Triangle' of embedded wireless connectivity, which trade-offs must an engineer balance? (Select all that apply)
options: Power consumption
Transmission range
Data bandwidth
Brand of solder used on the breadboard
explanation: RF physics mandates trade-offs between battery life (power), distance covered (range), and throughput (bandwidth).

prompt: What catastrophic hardware failure will occur if an engineer connects a 12V 500mA water pump motor directly to an ESP32 GPIO pin?
options: The motor will run backwards due to inverted logic.
The microcontroller GPIO will supply infinite power and trigger a brownout reset.
The GPIO pin (rated for ~12-20mA at 3.3V) and its internal transistors will burn out from massive overcurrent and inductive flyback.
The Wi-Fi antenna will overheat.
explanation: Microcontroller GPIO pins are low-current logic lines (max ~12-20mA). High current inductive loads must always be isolated with a MOSFET or relay.

prompt: An agricultural startup needs to deploy 50 soil-moisture probes across a 15-kilometer vineyard where cellular reception is spotty and each sensor must run for 4 years on two AA batteries. Which wireless technology is the optimal engineering choice?
scenarioContext: Coverage: 15km | Payload: 12 bytes every 30 minutes | Target Battery Life: 4 Years
options: High-speed 5G Cellular Modem
Wi-Fi 6 Mesh Network
LoRaWAN (Low Power Long Range)
Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR)
explanation: LoRaWAN delivers kilometer-scale range and multi-year battery longevity for minuscule payloads (few bytes per transmission).

prompt: What is the primary function of an ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) on a microcontroller?
options: It converts 240V AC grid electricity into 5V DC power.
It samples continuous analog voltage signals and quantizes them into discrete digital numerical integers.
It encrypts MQTT packets before sending them over the radio.
It converts Python source code into binary machine bytecode.
explanation: The ADC translates continuous real-world voltage levels into integer counts (e.g. 0 to 4095 on a 12-bit ADC).

prompt: Why is deep sleep mode essential for battery-powered remote IoT devices?
options: It reduces current consumption from tens of milliamperes down to microamperes while inactive, extending battery life by months or years.
It completely erases flash memory to prevent data theft.
It cools down the ambient air temperature around the sensor.
It increases the CPU clock speed to 1 Gigahertz.
explanation: In deep sleep, almost all internal peripherals and clock trees are disabled, sipping single-digit microamps of current.

prompt: A developer notes that their ESP32 analogRead() on pin 34 returns 4095 for a voltage of 3.3V, but returns 0 when the wire is disconnected entirely and floating in the air. Sometimes when hands touch the board, the reading fluctuates wildly between 400 and 2200. What circuit element is missing?
scenarioContext: Pin State: Floating high impedance input | Symptom: Random capacitive coupling
options: A cooling fan heatsink.
A pull-down (or pull-up) resistor to provide a stable reference voltage when disconnected.
A higher bitrate USB-C data cable.
A 100-watt transformer.
explanation: Floating input pins pick up ambient electromagnetic interference and stray capacitance. A pull-down or pull-up resistor clamps the pin to a known state when unasserted.
